# Derived, never hardcoded. This sat at 2.1.0 through the 3.0.0 AND 3.1.0 releases, so
# every install manifest -- the receipt `ck diff` and `ck uninstall` read for provenance --
# recorded a version two releases stale. It is the FIFTH version site; hard rule 7 named
# three, then four. The rule now points at the test rather than listing them, and the test
# reads this file.
VERSION="$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/pyproject.toml" | head -1)"
if [[ -z "$VERSION" ]]; then
    echo "FATAL: cannot read the version from pyproject.toml" >&2
    exit 1
fi

literal = re.compile(r'(?:__version__\s*=|return)\s+"(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)"')
    for py in (REPO / "src").rglob("*.py"):
        for found in literal.findall(py.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            assert found == version, (
                f"stale version literal {found!r} in {py}; pyproject says {version!r}")
    # install.sh too. Scanning only src/ is why `VERSION="2.1.0"` survived TWO releases
    # there unnoticed, stamping a stale version into every install manifest. Any literal
    # assignment is the defect; the value must be derived from pyproject.
    installer = (REPO / "install.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    hardcoded = re.findall(r'^VERSION="(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)"', installer, re.M)
    assert not hardcoded, (
        f"install.sh hardcodes VERSION={hardcoded[0]!r}; derive it from pyproject.toml")
